done.why: I ran out of turns just after the robot pushed the triangular button. I had the place mat, letter opener and newspaper with me and was heading for the barred door in the Tiny Room to get the blue sphere, and then the balloon.

about: A treasure hunt under the ground, on the Wizard of Frobozz's turf. He has squirreled away the Empire's lost valuables south of the ravine. You work through a run of linked tricks: a riddle door, a bucket that rises on water, Alice-style cakes, a lizard you bribe with candy, a dragon you trick into melting a glacier, and a princess whose unicorn hands over the key. Through all of it the Wizard keeps popping in to throw half-finished spells at you. It's also about putting up with a spinning room that won't let you choose where you go.

moments.note: A grue standing in the light. Examining it showed it was one of the Wizard's 'Fantasize' illusions, and the room is 'embarrassed' about it. Charming.
The Wizard's first visit doubles as a map of my goals: pearls behind a door that asks a question, then a room that won't keep still.
Answered the riddle with 'a well' and got a thunderclap and an open door.
Examining the bucket all but spelled out the puzzle: fresh water, from a ford, carried in a teapot. A fair, generous hint.
Spent many turns going in and out of the carousel trying to land in the Riddle Room. The rerolls felt like busywork.
Poured water in the bucket and rode it up: 'Well done.'
The red cake evaporated the pool of tears and uncovered the candy.
Pressed the triangular button myself and died on the spot. The robot was clearly there for that, but I got no warning beyond the DANGER sign.
Death sends you through coloured mist spheres to a face that promises to spare you 'this time'. A nice, eerie touch.
Found the lost candy lying in the carousel room after dying.
The dragon breathed fire at its own reflection in the ice and melted the glacier. The best payoff of the session.
The unicorn came to the princess, and she handed me the gold key and a rose.
The trophy cabinet holds my lost necklace but is 'protected by a fearful spell', so I can't store treasure there or get it back.
Smashed the aquarium with the sword and the serpent killed me. Nothing was in the tank afterwards, so that cost me a death for nothing.
Through the barred window, something round on a table 'takes the red light and gives it back blue'. A clear next goal.
The robot pressed the button and I heard a 'dull thump' far off. Probably the carousel stopping, but my turns ran out before I could check.

wished: Some way to pick a passage in the carousel room other than walking out and back in over and over
A warning that touching the buttons or breaking the aquarium would kill me outright, or a way to undo it
A way to store or get back treasures from the trophy cabinet
More turns, to open the barred door with the place mat and letter opener and to fly the balloon

lines.line: the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question, and the rest further in, past a room that will not keep still, which you will hear before you see it.
lines.why: It gave me my purpose and a rough map in one sentence.

lines.line: It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: A witty way to handle the Wizard's illusions, and it kept me from wasting time on them.

lines.line: Whatever it is that makes it go up, it will go up with what is in it and without what is not; that is the whole art of buckets.
lines.why: Lovely phrasing that also works as a hint.

lines.line: Dragons are smart, but sometimes naive, and this one has never seen ice before.
lines.why: The funniest and most satisfying puzzle solution I hit.

lines.line: "You may have use of such a thing," she says. "It is the least I can do for one who rescued me from a fate I dare not contemplate."
lines.why: The payoff for following the princess. It felt earned.

lines.line: There is something on the table, round, that takes the red light and gives it back blue.
lines.why: Set up the next goal clearly without naming it.

fun.why: The puzzle payoffs were great: the bucket, the cakes, the dragon and ice, the princess and unicorn. Two deaths that came out of nowhere and a lot of carousel rerolling took some of the fun out of it.

engagement.why: I always had a clear next goal and kept pushing until the turn cap stopped me mid-plan.

difficulty.why: The hints were fair and often generous, like the bucket description and the window. But the electrocution and the serpent killed me with no real warning, and the random carousel added grind rather than challenge.

interestingness.why: The puzzles chain into each other well. The Wizard's interruptions and the illusion objects that turn out never to have been there give the place character. Several systems interlock: death sends things to the cabinet, the princess walks off and you follow her footprints, the robot takes orders.

prose.why: Wry and precise, with descriptions that double as hints and some genuinely funny lines.
